clippings.speaker: David Fincher
clippings.quote: Sometimes I’d break Jeff off [on his own] and say, ‘Go across the street and find me a shot.’ I say this with humility: There aren’t a lot of people that I’d just [ask] to ‘go get me a shot.’ I’m not talking about trust so much as the knowledge that he wouldn’t need any handholding. I knew he’d come back with exactly what we needed.
clippings.title: Jeff Cronenweth, ASC: An Adventurous Eye
clippings.context: Fincher recalling Cronenweth operating on 2nd-unit reshoots for Seven, in an ASC career profile of the cinematographer.

clippings.speaker: David Fincher
clippings.quote: He might look at Fight Club as this big break, but I look at it as the natural evolution of what we were already doing. On Alien3, he and his father had been like one person.
clippings.title: Jeff Cronenweth, ASC: An Adventurous Eye
clippings.context: Fincher, calling Cronenweth "very humble," on handing him his first feature as cinematographer.

clippings.speaker: David Fincher
clippings.quote: I love when a cinematographer figures out a way to key someone without just setting a light and focusing it on them… The cinematographers I’ve always admired and worked with are very conscious of this. Jordan was excellent that way, and Jeff innately has that sensibility, too.
clippings.title: Jeff Cronenweth, ASC: An Adventurous Eye
clippings.context: Fincher comparing Jeff's lighting instincts to those of his father, Jordan Cronenweth.

clippings.speaker: Jeff Cronenweth
clippings.quote: Although I knew it would be rough, I had so much trust in David as a filmmaker that I had the confidence to do the film. He has such a distinct eye and is such a talented storyteller that the visuals in his films are always a collaboration in the truest sense.
clippings.title: Beyond The Frame: Fight Club
clippings.context: Retrospective drawing on AC's 1999 Fight Club feature, where Cronenweth discussed taking on his first feature with Fincher.

clippings.speaker: Jeff Cronenweth
clippings.quote: It would be tough for anybody to walk into a Fincher movie… When I met David in Zurich, he looked like he had been in a 12-round fight. He was beat just trying to keep up to the aesthetic level he was accustomed to; it was a lot of work.
clippings.film: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
clippings.title: Fincher's SOS to d.p. gets quick reply
clippings.context: Cronenweth on replacing the original DP mid-shoot on The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo.

clippings.speaker: Jeff Cronenweth
clippings.quote: Truly, not much has changed other than the ability to sleep a little more comfortably. I think we have become more decisive and efficient, but that could be as much about the years we have collaborated together and experience as it could be from the transformation to digital capture–or more likely a combination of both.
clippings.title: Road To Oscar Prequel: Artists On "Gone Girl," "Birdman" Emerging As Awards Season Contenders
clippings.context: Asked how his working relationship with Fincher had evolved, during Gone Girl's awards campaign.

clippings.speaker: Jeff Cronenweth
clippings.quote: Even from a time when I was a camera assistant and had the opportunity to work with him a few times, aesthetically we saw eye to eye. We kind of share some of the same sensibilities and that made it really easy each time to discover what it is that particular film’s language would be…
clippings.title: An Interview with Jeff Cronenweth
clippings.context: Cronenweth on the partnership in a career interview.

notes: Fincher rarely speaks about Cronenweth; all three Fincher quotes come from one 2022 ASC profile. The Fight Club quote is AC's 1999 interview as republished in a 2016 retrospective.
